title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

Figure 1 compares production budgets with worldwide box-office revenues. Each point represents one film, and both amounts are measured in millions of US dollars.

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Production budget (millions of US dollars)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Production budgets and worldwide revenues of films in the dataset.

title: Box Office Numbers
text:
This website explores a dataset of 104 well-known films released between 1980 and 2025. The dataset includes film titles, release years, franchises, production budgets, worldwide revenues, runtimes, and IMDb ratings. Budgets and revenues are approximate, measured in millions of US dollars, and not adjusted for inflation.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
Figure 1 compares film runtimes with IMDb ratings. Each point represents one film in the dataset.
plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating (0 to 10)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtimes and IMDb ratings.

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

The Bond films in this dataset were released from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Release year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of James Bond films by release year.
